document.title: Minutes of Conversation of General Secretary Brezhnev with Erich Honecker, October 4, 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Minutes of the Brezhnev-Honecker conversation. They shed light on Soviet geostrategic thinking about Afghanistan, the impact of the Iranian revolution, perceived U.S. goals, and suspected Amin-U.S. special services cooperation.

persons.name: Leonid Ilyich Brezhnev
persons.role: General Secretary of the CC CPSU and Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR

mentions.quote: GENERAL SECRETARY OF THE CC CPSU AND CHAIRMAN OF THE PRESIDIUM OF THE SUPREME SOVIET OF THE USSR, LEONID ILYICH BREZHNEV
I met him and advised him to take measures to stabilize the situation in his country

persons.name: Erich Honecker
persons.role: SED CC General Secretary and Chairman of the State Council (GDR)

mentions.quote: SED CC GENERAL SECRETARY AND CHAIRMAN OF THE STATE COUNCIL, ERICH HONECKER

persons.name: Hafizullah Amin
persons.role: Afghan leader who eliminated Taraki and took the leadership (Sept 1979)

mentions.quote: Amin has taken advantage of Taraki's indecisiveness and, as you know, eliminated him; he has achieved the leadership.
Frankly, we are not pleased by all of Amin's methods and actions. He is very power-driven.
Taraki had a stopover in Moscow on his way from Havana where the Conference of the Non-Alignment Movement took place.
the desire of Chancellor Schmidt to meet with you
Carter was left with nothing else but to retreat.

events.description: Brezhnev and Honecker meet in Berlin; Brezhnev briefs on Afghanistan, Iran, SALT II, missiles
Amin eliminates Taraki and takes leadership of Afghanistan
Brezhnev meets Taraki in Moscow on his return from the Havana NAM conference, advising stabilization measures
Brezhnev and Honecker meet in Berlin with Politburo members and Soviet delegation; Brezhnev briefs on missiles, SALT II, China, Iran, Afghanistan.
NATO meeting planned for December to decide on stationing new American medium-range missiles in Western Europe.
Amin eliminated Taraki and took Afghan leadership (recent event before Oct 1979).
Taraki stopped over in Moscow returning from the Non-Aligned Movement conference in Havana and met Brezhnev.
Soviet-Chinese negotiations on normalization of relations begin in Moscow.

key_claims: Brezhnev states Afghan rebels receive direct and indirect support from Pakistan and direct support from Iran, the USA and China.
Brezhnev says the USSR has supplied Afghanistan with economic aid, civilian and military advisers, and significant weapons.
Brezhnev admits Amin exploited Taraki's indecisiveness and eliminated him despite Soviet efforts to preserve Afghan leadership unity.
Brezhnev expresses reservations about Amin's harshness but says he remains committed to cooperation with the USSR.
Brezhnev commits to continued Soviet support against foreign aggression and domestic counterrevolution.
